title: Metric cardinality controls for tier/model/route SLO breakdowns (budgeted labels, sampling, aggregation)
creator: Aisha Bello
project: Tiered SLO definitions + error budget policy
description:
Context
- Tiered SLOs require consistent breakdowns by tier (Hosted/Dedicated), region, model, and route.
- Current metric label usage is trending toward unbounded cardinality (raw route paths, model revisions/aliases, customer IDs leaking into labels, etc.). This will (a) drive ingestion/query cost, (b) degrade dashboard/alert reliability, and (c) risk incorrect SLI calculations due to sparse series.

Goal
Keep required SLO dimensions (tier/region/model/route) within a defined cardinality budget per metric family while preserving enough fidelity for:
- SLO dashboards (per-tier, per-region, per-route)
- burn-rate alerts (multi-window)
- canary analysis (scoped to tier/service/route)

Non-goals
- Re-architecture of telemetry pipeline.
- Perfect per-customer dedicated breakdown in shared metrics (Dedicated customer-specific views will be handled via controlled backends / restricted queries).

Proposed cardinality budget (initial)
Applies to key SLO metric families in gateway + routing + runtime (request_count, error_count, latency_histogram, stream_disconnect_count):
- tier: max 2 values (hosted, dedicated)
- region: max ~15 (current prod regions)
- route: <= 50 canonical routes per service (normalized templates only; no raw paths)
- model: <= 30 per tier per region for ‘gold’ metrics; long-tail models aggregated into “other” for dashboards/alerts
- status_class: 5 values (2xx/3xx/4xx/5xx/timeout)
- error_class: bounded enum only (see SLI spec; no free-form strings)

Key decisions (need sign-off)
1) Route normalization
- Use route templates (e.g., /v1/chat/completions, /v1/embeddings) + method + streaming=true/false.
- Explicitly forbid raw paths, request IDs, or tool/function names in labels.

2) Model label policy
- Use stable model identifiers (e.g., catalog slug) not opaque revision IDs.
- For dashboards/alerts: maintain an allowlist of top-N models per tier/region (by request volume) emitted as model=<slug>; everything else emits model=other.
- For debugging: allow full model slug only in logs/traces, not in high-volume metrics.

3) Dedicated customer isolation
- Do NOT use customer_id / pool_id as a metric label in shared Prometheus-style metrics.
- Dedicated customer views should be produced via restricted backends (Console/ops) using scoped queries against logs/traces or a dedicated store with access control.

4) Sampling/aggregation
- For latency histograms at very high QPS routes, use:
  - per-route histograms only for canonical routes
  - aggregate across model=other
  - optional sampling for debug-only histograms (not used in SLO computation)

Implementation plan
Phase A — Audit + guardrails (this ticket)
- Inventory current label sets for the SLO-relevant metric families across gateway/routing/runtime.
- Identify top offenders by active series count and churn rate (series created/min).
- Add automated checks (CI or runtime startup warnings) to detect forbidden labels and route-template violations.

Phase B — Enforce bounded dimensions
- Implement route canonicalization in API Gateway instrumentation.
- Implement model allowlist/other bucketing in routing layer instrumentation.
- Remove/rename any high-card labels that slipped in (customer_id, request_id, raw_model_revision, raw_path).

Phase C — Documentation + operational playbook
- Publish “Metrics Labeling Standard for SLOs” (short doc + examples).
- Add oncall note: how to debug without high-card labels (logs/traces links).

Acceptance criteria
- Active series counts for each SLO metric family stay within budget in all prod regions for 7 consecutive days:
  - request_count: <= 50k active series
  - error_count: <= 50k active series
  - latency_histogram: <= 150k active series (bounded buckets * bounded labels)
  (Exact thresholds to be finalized w/ Logan/Nadia based on current ingestion limits.)
- Dashboards (ENG-2425) still support filtering by tier/region/route, and show top models without query timeouts.
- Burn-rate alerts (ENG-2420) evaluate successfully under load (no missing series, no 10m+ query times).
- SLI computations match validation queries within agreed tolerance (see scratchpad).

Risks / tradeoffs
- Bucketing models into “other” reduces model-specific visibility; mitigate with:
  - top-N allowlist
  - on-demand debug views via logs/traces
- Route canonicalization must be consistent across services; otherwise SLO rollups drift. We should treat route templates as an API contract between teams.

Owners / reviewers
- DRI: Thomas Baird
- Reviewers: Nadia Rahman (SLI correctness), Logan Wright (telemetry platform), Amara Diallo (gateway), Ravi Menon (routing), Sergio Costa (dashboards)

Notes
- Dedicated customer escalations (e.g., SUP-3911) are driving demand for per-customer breakdowns; we should meet that need via controlled views rather than exploding metric cardinality.
- This work is a prerequisite for scaling tier-aware SLOs to per-model/per-route without blowing up cost or alert quality.

Need final review from Amara + Ravi.
